recent_posts.title: Evolving Our License for Long-Term Sustainability
recent_posts.summary: Directus is transitioning from the Business Source License (BSL) to a new Monospace Sustainable Core License (MSCL) with the v12 release. The change separates the license from the usage grant to reduce ambiguity. Key points: organizations under $5M revenue and 50 employees get free full access via an Innovation Grant; a free Core tier remains available for larger organizations; every version automatically converts to GPLv3 after 4 years; software registration keys replace the previous honor system; and SDKs remain MIT-licensed. The only restriction is building a competing product.

recent_posts.title: Using Directus MCP and AI to migrate a legacy database in a weekend
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares how they used Directus with its MCP (Model Context Protocol) server and an LLM (Claude) to dramatically reduce a complex legacy CMS database migration from 5-8 weeks to 2-3 days. The approach involves installing Directus on top of the existing database, letting the AI analyze schema and generate JSON mapping files, then having a human review and confirm each configuration before applying changes via scripts with dry-run support. The key insight is keeping humans in control while offloading the tedious analysis and boilerplate generation to AI.

recent_posts.title: Directus v11.17: Background Imports, Netlify Deployments, and a Translations Generator
recent_posts.summary: Directus v11.17 introduces background data imports that prevent large CSV/dataset imports from blocking the UI, with configurable timeouts and concurrency limits. Netlify is now supported in the deployment module alongside Vercel, enabling content teams to trigger deploys directly from the Data Studio. A new translations generator scaffolds the full i18n setup (collections, junctions, relationships) in seconds instead of 10-15 minutes. The Tabs group interface is now built into core, replacing the community extension. Additional improvements include AI Assistant observability via Braintrust and Langfuse, Anthropic tool search, comparison modal filtering for modified fields only, Redis namespace control, a cache clear CLI command, GraphQL resolver deduplication, and timezone support for datetime fields. Extension developers should note a breaking UI resize from px to rem units.

recent_posts.title: Leap Week 4 Highlights
recent_posts.summary: Directus held a three-day 'Leap Week' event featuring nine live sessions covering the shifting role of UI in software, AI in the enterprise, live build demos, and partner sessions with Railway, Clay, and Firecrawl. Sessions included a keynote on UI's declining role as a differentiator, a live frontend build-off on top of Directus, a discussion on enterprise AI with HelloFresh and Gather.dev, and the announcement of the Directus Builders community program. All recordings are available on Directus TV.

recent_posts.title: Jira Data Center EOL: What Operational Platform Builders Should Do Now
recent_posts.summary: Jira Data Center reached end-of-new-sales on March 30, 2026, with full EOL in March 2029. Many enterprises unknowingly built operational data platforms on top of Jira DC using custom fields, ScriptRunner automations, and direct DB access — making migration far more complex than switching project trackers. Three customer categories are outlined: agile shops (move to Jira Cloud or Linear), compliance-constrained enterprises (need contingency plans before March 2028 license renewal deadline), and 'Category 3' operational platform builders who need a structured data layer with APIs, access control, and self-hosted deployment. Directus is presented as a migration target for Category 3 teams, offering automatic REST/GraphQL APIs on any SQL database, a no-code admin UI, field-level permissions, workflow automation (Flows), and full self-hosting. A practical 5-step migration path is outlined, and organizations are urged to begin evaluation immediately given that serious data platform migrations in regulated environments take 12–18 months.

recent_posts.title: Directus v11.16: Global Draft Versions, Multimodal AI, and Smarter Deployments
recent_posts.summary: Directus v11.16 introduces global draft versions that automatically apply to every versioned item without manual setup, eliminating per-item version creation friction. The AI Assistant gains multimodal capabilities, allowing users to upload images and PDFs directly into conversations, with support across OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini. The deployment module now supports role-based access control so non-admin team members can trigger deploys, and real-time status updates via Vercel and Netlify webhooks replace polling. A new json() query function lets developers extract specific values from JSON columns at the API level across all supported databases. Additional improvements include persisted table column widths, MIME type restrictions for file interfaces, auth audit hooks, and several bug fixes.

recent_posts.title: Directus v11.15: Native Collaborative Editing, AI Assistant Goes GA, and One-Click Deployments
recent_posts.summary: Directus v11.15 introduces native collaborative editing with real-time presence indicators and field-level locking, eliminating save conflicts when multiple users edit the same record. The AI Assistant reaches general availability with multi-provider support (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Ollama), context-aware responses from content items and visual editor elements, and a dedicated sidebar for live preview editing. A new deployment module enables one-click Vercel deployments directly from the Data Studio, with deployment monitoring and log access. Additional improvements include revision-to-revision comparison, relational fields on bar charts, and clearer permission-blocked field appearance.

recent_posts.title: How I Built an Employee Advocacy Scoreboard with Directus, Zapier, and Claude Code
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step walkthrough of building an automated employee advocacy tracking system. The solution uses Slack for link submission, Zapier with GPT-4o-mini for AI-powered link detection and data cleaning, Directus as a headless CMS backend, and a Next.js dashboard scaffolded with Claude Code. The system automatically captures social media posts from team members, validates and cleans the data, stores it in Directus, and displays a leaderboard with monthly filtering and individual drill-downs.

recent_posts.title: Hello from Directus' New VP of Engineering
recent_posts.summary: David Stockton introduces himself as Directus' new VP of Engineering, sharing his journey from childhood programming on a Commodore 64 through a 25-year career in software engineering and leadership roles. Most recently Director of Cloud Infrastructure Engineering at Confluent, he managed globally distributed teams overseeing thousands of Kubernetes clusters. He joined Directus for the team and opportunity to contribute to their API-first data platform, which he sees as well-positioned for AI-driven development needs.

recent_posts.title: Directus v11.14: AI Chat Beta, Bulk Downloads + More
recent_posts.summary: Directus 11.14 introduces external JWT validation for integrating with enterprise IAM providers like Okta and Auth0, enabling scope-based permission mapping and eliminating manual token management. The release adds bulk file and folder downloads as ZIP archives, a Header interface for organizing complex forms, and a beta AI chat sidebar with resizable workspace panels. Breaking changes include removal of sidebar states from the app store, requiring extension updates.

top_posts.title: REST vs. GraphQL vs. tRPC: Choosing Your API Architecture
top_posts.summary: Choosing the right API architecture is crucial for your team's productivity. REST is reliable and widely compatible, GraphQL is good for complex data requirements, and tRPC is ideal for TypeScript environments. The best choice depends on your team's expertise, project scope, and performance needs, and sometimes a mix of these technologies works best.

top_posts.title: Stop Overengineering Your Multi-tenant Architecture
top_posts.summary: Multi-tenancy is crucial for building SaaS products. Simplified, it can cut infrastructure costs significantly. Three main approaches exist: row-level tenancy, schema-level separation, and database-level isolation. Start simple and scale as needed, with row-level tenancy sufficing for most starting apps. Tools like Flyway or Liquibase for migrations, PostgreSQL for database, and PgBouncer for connection management are recommended.

top_posts.title: Solving the Multiple-Frontend Problem in Modern Applications
top_posts.summary: Modern applications often require multiple frontend architectures to support various platforms like web, mobile, and IoT. This post discusses practical approaches to manage multiple frontends without resorting to rewriting the entire codebase or learning new frameworks. Key strategies include adopting an API-first approach and using Module Federation to share code efficiently. It also covers the importance of finding natural boundaries based on business logic, handling the performance paradox, ensuring security, and managing integration points effectively.

top_posts.summary: Learn how to implement Directus Auth in Next.js 14, register new users, and perform CRUD operations on posts.

top_posts.title: Building a Job Board Platform with Directus and SolidStart.js
top_posts.summary: Learn how to build a fully functional job board platform combining Directus's backend capabilities with SolidStart.js' reactive frontend. This guide covers user registration, authentication, job listing management, and application processes. You'll set up a Directus project with necessary data models, configure user roles and permissions, and integrate frontend functionalities using SolidStart.js.
